index 85af9adc..3e1e0e38 100644
--- a/outlines/types/__init__.py
+++ b/outlines/types/__init__.py
@@ -52,6 +52,10 @@ whitespace = Regex(r"\s")
 sentence = Regex(r"[A-Z].*\s*[.!?]")
 paragraph = Regex(rf"{sentence.pattern}(?:\s+{sentence.pattern})*\n+")
 
+# A SHA-256 digest written as exactly 64 hexadecimal characters, in any case.
+# Validation uses a full match, so surrounding whitespace is refused.
+hash_sha256 = Regex(r"[a-fA-F0-9]{64}")
+
 
 # The following regex is FRC 5322 compliant and was found at:
 # https://emailregex.com/
@@ -68,3 +72,14 @@ email = Regex(
 isbn = Regex(
     r"(?:ISBN(?:-1[03])?:? )?(?=[0-9X]{10}$|(?=(?:[0-9]+[- ]){3})[- 0-9X]{13}$|97[89][0-9]{10}$|(?=(?:[0-9]+[- ]){4})[- 0-9]{17}$)(?:97[89][- ]?)?[0-9]{1,5}[- ]?[0-9]+[- ]?[0-9]+[- ]?[0-9X]"
 )
+
+# Matches a 16-digit credit card number written as four groups of four digits.
+# The groups are either joined with no separator at all, or all separated by a
+# space, or all separated by a hyphen; mixing separators ("1234-5678 9012-3456")
+# is rejected. The alternatives are spelled out because the regex DSL is
+# compiled to a finite state machine, which cannot express a backreference to
+# "the separator used so far". This only checks the shape of the number: it
+# does not verify the Luhn check digit or the card network's prefix.
+credit_card = Regex(
+    r"[0-9]{16}|[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}|[0-9]{4} [0-9]{4} [0-9]{4} [0-9]{4}"
